headline: Micron has settled its patent fight with Netlist by taking a five-year licence and agreeing to pay about $600 million.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a sizeable settlement tied to AI memory technology, from a trade outlet quoting the company.
importance_line: It ends a dispute for Micron at the price of a recurring licence cost and shows Netlist now collecting from all three big memory makers, but the report gives no effect on memory prices, and Netlist still has a case against Google.
summary: Blocks & Files reports that Micron and Netlist have settled their patent litigation, with Micron taking a five-year licence to Netlist's memory technology, paying $30 million a quarter until the third quarter of 2031 (about $600 million in licence fees) and buying $1 million of Netlist stock. It follows Samsung's August agreement to pay Netlist $897 million over five years, which leaves Netlist with disputes against Micron, Samsung and SK hynix won or settled for licence fees valued at $1.54 billion, the outlet says.
notes: Full text read. Text calls the Samsung deal 'just 3 months ago' though it also says August; we say August. Micron's own statement not seen.
